text:
adele: quick heads-up — completed a first canary run for raptor-1q (int8) on raven infra and we have a small but notable uptick in function-call JSON parse failures. baseline model was ~0.08%, raptor is ~0.9% across 20k canary requests. samples below. :eyes:

adele: sample bad payloads (copied directly from model stdout):
```
{"action":"create_ticket","params":{"title":"DB outage","service":"payments"}

ERROR: stream ended
```

and

```
{"action":"set_status","params":{"ticket_id":1234,"status":"in_progress"}  <-- missing closing brace
```

ryan: do we know if these correlate with streaming responses or batch sizes? could be stream boundaries truncating JSON. any differences between batch=1 vs batch>1?

adele: initial canary config: model=raptor-1q-int8, temperature=0.02, top_p=0.95, batch_size=8, streaming=true, prefix_cache=true, max_new_tokens=128. failures jump when batch_size>1 and streaming=true. batch_size=1 + streaming still has a few but much lower.

jess: sounds like streaming + batching is the suspect. two quick mitigations: 1) disable streaming for canary traffic (serialize full output) or 2) wrap outputs in an explicit fence on generation side (e.g., emit ```json
...
```) so postprocessors can trim noise. also add a fast JSON-repair fallback that tries to close brackets/braces and strip trailing logs before parse.

kiran: agree. also want to check tokenization boundary: maybe quantization changed EOS behavior. can you paste raw token ids + decoding debug for a few failing requests? even 10 samples would help.

adele: grabbing token logs now. quick sample token decode snippet:
```
tokens: [1045, 32, 123, 34, 97, 99, 116, 105, 111, 110, 34, 58, 34, 99, 114, 101, 97, 116, 101, 95, 116, 105, 99, 107, 101, 116, 34, 125, 13]
decoded: '{"action":"create_ticket"}\r'  <-- stray carriage return
```

ryan: stray CR/linebreaks are common when streaming gets interleaved with logs. Could also be that quantized tokenizer emits different whitespace for EOS. Two experiments: A) run canary with streaming=false; B) run streaming + batch=1. if failures drop to baseline in one of those, we isolate it.

jess: for medium-term, add a small parser wrapper on the service side that: 1) strips non-JSON leading/trailing lines, 2) tries simple repairs (balance braces, remove trailing non-ASCII), 3) runs a strict json.loads. log original+repaired for telemetry. we already have a tiny library for this in devex -> maybe reuse.

adele: plan: 1) roll canary to stop streaming for 1 hour (A) 2) run streaming+b1 (B) 3) collect 10k requests each and compare funcall_parse_failure metric. i'm going to tag the canary job. kiran can you add metric tag funcall_parse_failure and a histogram of truncated_length?

kiran: added metric tag and a small probe to record trailing_char_samples. will also surface token-id diffs for failing vs passing.

ci-bot: CI: canary-run-2182009876 scheduled (jobs: raptor-int8-canary-A, raptor-int8-canary-B).

adele: thanks — i'll also start a small local repro harness that replays failing token sequences with deterministic seeds. jess, can you fork the devex json-repair lib and add a flag to enable/disable aggressive fixes so we can A/B? :hammer:

jess: yep doing that now. will push a branch and link once ready. i'll include a small eval that measures false-positive repairs on a held-out set.

ryan: nice. once we confirm isolation, we should add a runtime guard in the serving runtime to disable streaming for known funcall endpoints, or auto-fence outputs for tool-call mode.

adele: agreed. will update after the two runs finish (expect results in ~2 hours). leaving logs in the canary artifact bucket under /canaries/raptor-2182009876/.
